titleEn: The Lake Is a Giant Bathtub!

pages.text: "I won't wash!" Nils the little bear ran to lakeside grass. Grandpa Bruno stood with a dry towel. Nils called, "If I go in, water gets on my head!"
All day, Nils had run dirt paths and rolled in grass. "Washing is boring. I'll play until dinner!" He flopped onto the grass.
But his back was sticky, damp in summer sun. Dry grass seeds and pine pollen stuck in his fur. Nils rubbed his back hard on a tree. "Itchy..."
Scratching kept him from running. Lake water rippled by his feet. Grandpa removed his blue boots and set them side by side. "Know this is the world's biggest bathtub?"
"Bathtub? The lake?" Nils sprang up. Grandpa strode into the water and spread his paws. "Only where my paw can reach. Just this far."
Nils dipped his toes gently. Lukewarm and refreshing. One step, two. Water rippled at his knees! "The lake is a giant bathtub!" He splashed.
Grandpa scooped water over Nils's back and rubbed. Grass seeds and pine pollen floated up. "The lake is a giant bathtub!" Nils laughed.
Out of the water, he felt fresh all over. Sitting on a warm stone, his fur dried fluffy. "All the itching went away!" Nils stood proud.
The next evening, Nils led the way to the water. "One, boots off, side by side! Two, only where Grandpa's paw can reach! Three, rub my back!" Both paws high! "The lake is a giant bathtub!"
Grandpa wrapped him in a dry towel and rubbed his back. Washing isn't something to endure; it's playing in water. Smiling inside the towel, Nils said, "The lake is a giant bathtub! Again tomorrow!"
